description: Official public behavior pycubrid claims to match or deliberately deviate from, each backed by a live differential case in tests/test_official_differential.py (#446). Observations are rendered as type-tagged strings, e.g. int(1) or (str('a'),).

claims.summary: A stored INTEGER value fetches with the same Python type and value as CUBRIDdb.
A stored BIGINT maximum fetches with the same Python type and value as CUBRIDdb.
A stored NUMERIC(10,2) value fetches as the same Decimal as CUBRIDdb.
A stored DOUBLE value fetches as the same float as CUBRIDdb.
A stored CHAR(5) value fetches with the same blank padding as CUBRIDdb.
A stored VARCHAR value fetches as the same str as CUBRIDdb.
A stored DATE value fetches as the same datetime.date as CUBRIDdb.
A stored TIME value fetches as the same datetime.time as CUBRIDdb.
A stored DATETIME value fetches as the same datetime.datetime as CUBRIDdb.
A stored JSON value fetches as the same raw str as CUBRIDdb.
A stored MONETARY value keeps its fraction in pycubrid; CUBRIDdb truncates it to int.
claims.reason: pycubrid decodes MONETARY to a value-preserving float; the official wrapper returns an int without the fraction. Copying the truncation would lose data.

claims.summary: A static multi-type scalar SELECT (INTEGER, BIGINT, NUMERIC, DOUBLE, VARCHAR, CHAR, DATE, NULL) returns the same row tuple as CUBRIDdb.
For the static scalar SELECT, description name, type_code, precision and scale (fields 0, 1, 4, 5) equal CUBRIDdb's in value and Python type.
Ordinary pycubrid reports display_size/internal_size as None and null_ok as bool; CUBRIDdb reports 0, 0 and an int.
claims.reason: The approved #438 compatibility contract keeps the documented 1.x ordinary description (None size fields, Boolean null_ok); only a future explicit wrapper namespace may return the native 0/0/int shape.

claims.summary: One prepared INTEGER SELECT handle re-executed with INT32 minimum, zero and maximum binds returns the same execute counts and fetch_row tuples as _cubrid.
One prepared VARCHAR SELECT handle re-executed with quote/backslash/Korean and empty string binds returns the same results as _cubrid.
A prepared two-parameter INSERT re-executed under the default autocommit returns the same counts as _cubrid, and an independent connection sees the same rows.
bind_param(1, None) binds SQL NULL in pycubrid; the official native bind_param raises SystemError.
claims.scenario_gap: No pinned upstream scenario binds None; the native failure was measured by #439.
claims.reason: The official extension returns NULL from bind_param without setting an exception (SystemError). The #439 compatibility cursor deliberately binds explicit SQL NULL instead of reproducing the crash-shaped failure.

claims.summary: imports(('3', '1', '3', '2'), INT) bound with bind_set into a SET(INTEGER) column stores the same deduplicated integers as _cubrid.
claims.scenario_gap: Upstream collection scenarios (tests3/test_set.py, tests2/python/_09_unittest/set.py) use the wrapper execute(query, args, set_type)/executemany shapes, tracked by #610; no pinned scenario calls native imports/bind_set directly. Measured by #440.

claims.summary: imports(('b', 'a', '한', 'b'), STRING) bound with bind_set into a SET(VARCHAR) column stores the same strings as _cubrid.
claims.scenario_gap: Upstream collection scenarios (tests3/test_set.py, tests2/python/_09_unittest/set.py) use the wrapper execute(query, args, set_type)/executemany shapes, tracked by #610; no pinned scenario calls native imports/bind_set directly. Measured by #440.

claims.summary: Like _cubrid, imports(('1', '2'), INT) sends STRING (2) elements whatever the requested element type, so an untyped SET column stores the strings '1' and '2', not integers. The default kind=SET request bytes equal the captured official bytes (tests/test_compat_collections.py).
claims.scenario_gap: Upstream collection scenarios (tests3/test_set.py, tests2/python/_09_unittest/set.py) use the wrapper execute(query, args, set_type)/executemany shapes, tracked by #610; no pinned scenario calls native imports/bind_set directly. Measured by #440.

claims.summary: imports((), INT) binds an empty SET, stored as an empty set, as in _cubrid.
claims.scenario_gap: Upstream collection scenarios (tests3/test_set.py, tests2/python/_09_unittest/set.py) use the wrapper execute(query, args, set_type)/executemany shapes, tracked by #610; no pinned scenario calls native imports/bind_set directly. Measured by #440.

claims.summary: bind_set with a set that was never imported binds SQL NULL, as in _cubrid.
claims.scenario_gap: Upstream collection scenarios (tests3/test_set.py, tests2/python/_09_unittest/set.py) use the wrapper execute(query, args, set_type)/executemany shapes, tracked by #610; no pinned scenario calls native imports/bind_set directly. Measured by #440.

claims.summary: bind_set(1, ('1',)) with a tuple instead of a set, and imports(['1'], INT) with a list instead of a tuple, both raise InterfaceError, as in _cubrid.
claims.scenario_gap: Upstream collection scenarios (tests3/test_set.py, tests2/python/_09_unittest/set.py) use the wrapper execute(query, args, set_type)/executemany shapes, tracked by #610; no pinned scenario calls native imports/bind_set directly. Measured by #440.

claims.summary: With kind=MULTISET, a MULTISET(INTEGER) column keeps duplicates ([1, 3, 3]); _cubrid has no kind and always binds a SET, which drops them ([1, 3]).
claims.scenario_gap: Upstream collection scenarios (tests3/test_set.py, tests2/python/_09_unittest/set.py) use the wrapper execute(query, args, set_type)/executemany shapes, tracked by #610; no pinned scenario calls native imports/bind_set directly. Measured by #440.
claims.reason: The official bind_set always sends the SET kind, so duplicates are lost silently. The broker rejects the MULTISET bind kind (-454), so pycubrid sends kind=MULTISET as SEQUENCE, which the server stores into a MULTISET column with its duplicates. The default kind=SET keeps the official bytes and result.

claims.summary: With kind=SEQUENCE, a SEQUENCE(INTEGER) column keeps order and duplicates ([3, 1, 3, 2]); _cubrid always binds a SET, which sorts and deduplicates ([1, 2, 3]).
claims.scenario_gap: Upstream collection scenarios (tests3/test_set.py, tests2/python/_09_unittest/set.py) use the wrapper execute(query, args, set_type)/executemany shapes, tracked by #610; no pinned scenario calls native imports/bind_set directly. Measured by #440.
claims.reason: The official bind_set always sends the SET kind, so order and duplicates are lost silently. kind=SEQUENCE is an explicit pycubrid extension; the default kind=SET keeps the official bytes and result.

claims.summary: The element 'NULL' stays the string 'NULL' in pycubrid; _cubrid turns it into a NULL element.
claims.scenario_gap: Upstream collection scenarios (tests3/test_set.py, tests2/python/_09_unittest/set.py) use the wrapper execute(query, args, set_type)/executemany shapes, tracked by #610; no pinned scenario calls native imports/bind_set directly. Measured by #440.
claims.reason: The official imports() treats the text 'NULL' as a NULL element, so the string 'NULL' cannot be stored. pycubrid uses None for a NULL element (same bytes) and keeps 'NULL' as text.

claims.summary: An empty string element is stored in pycubrid; _cubrid's imports() raises InterfaceError for it.
claims.scenario_gap: Upstream collection scenarios (tests3/test_set.py, tests2/python/_09_unittest/set.py) use the wrapper execute(query, args, set_type)/executemany shapes, tracked by #610; no pinned scenario calls native imports/bind_set directly. Measured by #440.
claims.reason: The official imports() rejects any empty element. An empty string is a valid VARCHAR value, so pycubrid sends it.

claims.summary: imports((1, 2), INT) accepts Python int elements in pycubrid and sends their decimal text (the official '1', '2' bytes); _cubrid raises InterfaceError for non-str elements.
claims.scenario_gap: Upstream collection scenarios (tests3/test_set.py, tests2/python/_09_unittest/set.py) use the wrapper execute(query, args, set_type)/executemany shapes, tracked by #610; no pinned scenario calls native imports/bind_set directly. Measured by #440.
claims.reason: Accepting int elements for the INT element type is an additive convenience: the request bytes equal the official call with digit strings, so no stored result differs.

claims.summary: imports(('1.5', '2'), NUMERIC) is accepted like any element type code other than BIT/VARBIT, sent as STRING elements, and stored into a SET(NUMERIC(5,2)) column as the same Decimals as _cubrid.
claims.scenario_gap: Upstream collection scenarios (tests3/test_set.py, tests2/python/_09_unittest/set.py) use the wrapper execute(query, args, set_type)/executemany shapes, tracked by #610; no pinned scenario calls native imports/bind_set directly. Measured by #440.

claims.summary: An element containing NUL raises ProgrammingError in pycubrid before any I/O; _cubrid silently truncates it at the NUL ('a\x00b' is stored as 'a').
claims.scenario_gap: Upstream collection scenarios (tests3/test_set.py, tests2/python/_09_unittest/set.py) use the wrapper execute(query, args, set_type)/executemany shapes, tracked by #610; no pinned scenario calls native imports/bind_set directly. Measured by #440.
claims.reason: The official imports() copies elements as C strings, so text after a NUL is lost silently. pycubrid rejects the element instead of storing a different value.

claims.summary: Failure classes for a float element, a bytes element, bind_set index 0 and 5 (one parameter), set(object()) and a server conversion error (-494) are ProgrammingError, ProgrammingError, ProgrammingError, ProgrammingError, InterfaceError and ProgrammingError in pycubrid; _cubrid raises InterfaceError x4, TypeError and IntegrityError.
claims.scenario_gap: Upstream collection scenarios (tests3/test_set.py, tests2/python/_09_unittest/set.py) use the wrapper execute(query, args, set_type)/executemany shapes, tracked by #610; no pinned scenario calls native imports/bind_set directly. Measured by #440.
claims.reason: pycubrid keeps the classes of its existing #439 prepared cursor: invalid values and indexes are ProgrammingError, a non-connection owner is InterfaceError, and server error -494 follows the driver-wide errno mapping (ProgrammingError) rather than the official extension's IntegrityError list. Every client-side failure happens before I/O and leaves the set and slot unchanged.

expected.pycubrid: [str('raises ProgrammingError'), str('raises ProgrammingError'), str('raises ProgrammingError'), str('raises ProgrammingError'), str('raises InterfaceError'), str('raises ProgrammingError')]
expected.native: [str('raises InterfaceError'), str('raises InterfaceError'), str('raises InterfaceError'), str('raises InterfaceError'), str('raises TypeError'), str('raises IntegrityError')]
